assessments.summary: Valid as a conditional claim. Assuming exactly the encoded and displayed Theorem 9 outer-bound premise, setting R0=0 and expanding each minimum and both interval side conditions yields exactly 30 scalar rows: 18 from six three-branch constraints, 4 from (19k)–(19l), 4 from (19m)–(19p), and 4 from the two interval conditions. The audited rows contain receiver terms involving only one of Y, G, K, or Z at a time, so replacing the auxiliary-receiver law by the product of its input-only G- and K-marginals preserves every joint marginal needed by every mutual-information term and hence preserves the full system. The resulting fixed-receiver optimization gives R1+R2 <= V(q;G,K) <= B(G,K) for every finite-output binary-input pair, implying the stated infimum upper bound on physical-BSSC sum capacity without interchanging supremum and infimum. Restricting to Q-supported hierarchies gives V_Q(G,K) <= V(1/2;G,K) <= B(G,K), including under sup(empty set)=-infinity. For Q0={0,1/2,1}, the endpoint information functions vanish, so all audited terms depend on each receiver only through its value at input prior 1/2; for the physical receivers these values are both c, yielding dependence only on (c,g,k,c). A concrete zero-rate Q0-supported hierarchy establishes nonemptiness, while individual-rate rows bound each rate by 1, so V_0(g,k) is finite and realization-independent on the realizable domain.
scopeQualifications: The result is conditional on the explicitly assumed Theorem 9 premise; it does not prove that theorem or authenticate its cited manuscript source.
No PDF-origin, source-fidelity, rendering, or visual-semantic assertion is established.
The capacity conclusion is an upper-bound formula, not an unconditional numerical evaluation of that infimum.
The well-definedness and finiteness of V_0(g,k) apply on the realizable (g,k)-domain.
